note: Faithful rendering of the commentary's lamp simile and the root-verse glosses; some clumsy doubled glosses but no substantive error.

errors.english: the character of the process [note: Tibetan: lugs su 'byung ba]
errors.why: lugs su 'byung ba is the forward order (anuloma) of dependent origination, contrasted on the previous side with the reverse order (lugs las bzlog pa); 'process' and the gloss lose that technical sense, and the later note '[Madhyamaka] system' misreads 'di'i ('of this eightfold dependent origination').

note: Argument comparing eightfold dependent origination with the twelve links is followed correctly; one technical term flattened.

errors.english: And the methods that cleanse the stains of the (kleshas) mental afflictions,
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of means that are themselves stained by (involve) the afflictions, not means that cleanse afflictive stains.

note: The siddhas' dohā verses are rendered verse by verse and accurately apart from one line.
Mudrā instructions, consecrations and the chapter colophon are rendered faithfully.

errors.english: May I give rise to all those miraculous powers.
errors.why: 'tshal ba here means to know/understand: 'may I come to know all their emanations', not produce them.

note: A sound rendering of the Bhadracarī verses; one verb misread.

errors.english: The syllable (ba) part of the cry of lamentation is the sound of (kyema) alas/how tragic.
errors.why: བ is just the end of རྗེས་སུ་བརྩེ་བ from the previous side ('in the sense of compassion, it is the exclamation kye ma'); there is no 'syllable ba' or 'part of the cry'.

fix.find: The syllable (ba) part of the cry of lamentation is the sound of (kyema) alas/how tragic.
fix.replace: [In the sense of compassion,] it is the exclamation (kye ma), "alas."

errors.english: It should be understood as "The practitioner spoke in this way."
errors.why: The honorific gsungs and the following gloss of the mantra-collection (sngags bsdus pa) show the clause is about the (Blessed One) speaking such a mantra-collection, not the practitioner speaking.

note: Mostly followable, but it invents a gloss at the opening and assigns the mantra-collection's utterance to the practitioner.

errors.english: To this, he says: "in that very context."
errors.why: de nyid du na is 'in reality' (tattvataḥ), the key qualifier of the Buddhist reply that ascertaining cognition has no real object.

errors.english: Then, if the pervader in the kitchen is apprehended, the pervaded will not be apprehended. If it is asked: "Even if it is not apprehended, does it not remain the pervader in reality?"
errors.why: This is one objection: 'when apprehending the pervader in the kitchen one need not apprehend the pervaded, since even unapprehended its being the pervader in reality is not lost'; the English splits it into a statement plus a separate question.

errors.english: If that were the case, he says: "Thus is the established conclusion."
errors.why: The commentary says the lemma 'de lta na ni' introduces the (author's) conclusion; the English turns the label 'conclusion' into a quoted root phrase.

note: The Pramāṇa argument is broadly tracked, but several objection/reply and lemma boundaries are blurred.

errors.english: This view involves a functional basis where patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision result only in fruitless exhaustion.
errors.why: The five (kṣānti, ruci, mati, prekṣā, dṛṣṭi) are the standard synonyms defining the view itself; its function (las) is to be the basis of fruitless toil.

fix.find: This view involves a functional basis where patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision result only in fruitless exhaustion.
fix.replace: It is the acceptance, inclination, opinion, conception, or view [that so regards them]; its function is to serve as the basis for fruitless toil.

errors.english: it is the destruction of existing things by denigrating the cause, the effect, or the activity.
errors.why: Denigrating cause, effect or activity and destroying existing things are four parallel kinds of wrong conceptualization (the text later illustrates 'destroying existing things' separately with 'there are no arhats').

fix.find: it is the destruction of existing things by denigrating the cause, the effect, or the activity.
fix.replace: it is any wrong conceptualization that denigrates the cause, the effect, or the activity, or that destroys existing things.

errors.tibetan: བཟོད་པ་དང་། འདོད་པ་དང་། བློ་གྲོས་དང་། རྟོག་པ་དང་། ལྟ་བ་དང་། དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་ཀུན་དུ་གཅོད་པའི་ལས་ཅན་དང་།
errors.english: Engaging in patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision that sever all roots of virtue.
errors.why: Again the five are synonyms of the wrong view itself; its first function is severing the roots of virtue.

fix.find: Engaging in patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision that sever all roots of virtue.
fix.replace: Severing the roots of virtue (the view itself being the acceptance, inclination, opinion, conception, or view [of such a wrong conceptualization]).

note: The examples of denigration are right, but the Abhidharma definitional formula (the five synonyms of view, and the four kinds of wrong view) is mis-segmented twice.

errors.english: regarding the white aspect of the (bodhicitta) awakening mind/vital essence
errors.why: dkar po'i phyogs is the bright (waxing) fortnight, paired with nag po (the dark half) below: bodhicitta moves upward from the left big toe through the lunar days of the bright half.

note: The laughter, Abhidhāna quotations and lunar-day circulation of bodhicitta are rendered accurately apart from the fortnight term.
The element maṇḍalas at the four lotuses, their functions and the inner homa substances are rendered faithfully.
